description: renew-microsoft-calendar-webhooks runs as a tenant-scoped EE maintenance fan-out job every 30 minutes with a 180 minute look-ahead, registered through the fan-out catalog and job registry (or defineJob if the name collision rule allows).
prdRefs: Schedule the renewal through the maintenance fan-out

description: A TenantSelector narrows the renewal fan-out to tenants with an active Microsoft calendar provider.
prdRefs: Schedule the renewal through the maintenance fan-out

description: One provider-level Microsoft delta sync operation (fetch from stored deltaLink, reset when invalid, persist the new deltaLink, apply changes) is extracted from CalendarWebhookProcessor.processMicrosoftWebhook and used by the webhook processor.
CalendarWebhookMaintenanceService runs the delta sync operation after it recreates a subscription (not after an ordinary renewal) and reports the catch-up result.
isResourceNotFoundError decides on HTTP status and Graph error code instead of matching '404' anywhere in the message.
A provider that cannot be recovered (for example a revoked refresh token) ends in the existing health/error path without failing the tenant run or other providers.
The Temporal calendar webhook maintenance workflow, stub activity, their index exports and the client start helper are deleted.
setupSchedules no longer creates calendar-webhook-maintenance-schedule and deletes the existing one with deleteScheduleIfExists.

The server-suite parity test requires every recurring registered handler name to be in the EE maintenance catalog or in an explicit commented exemption list; renew-microsoft-calendar-webhooks is not exempt.
